rounds.text: Bhartiya International Ltd is fundamentally undervalued based on a DCF model that calculates an intrinsic value of Rs 1154 per share against a market price of Rs 962, leaving a margin of safety of 16.6% [E45, E46]. The company exhibits robust top-line acceleration, delivering a 32% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a 20% compounded sales growth over 5 years, easily outpacing the sector median sales growth of 17.4% [E15, E17, E74]. Profit growth is equally compelling, highlighted by a 33% compounded profit growth over 5 years and a 31% expansion over the trailing twelve months, which substantially outstrips the sector median profit growth of 12.2% [E19, E21, E73]. Furthermore, insiders are backing the business aggressively, with promoters increasing their stake to 61.17% in Sep 2026 from 57.35% in Dec 2023 [E41], and cash conversion stands at a healthy 1.46x with profits fully backed by cash [E34]. Conceded: [E4] dividend yield is 0.00%, [E20] compounded profit growth over 3 years is -40%, and [E37] debt to equity is 1.16x indicating leverage risk.

Bhartiya International Ltd carries significant valuation and leverage risks that the current price fails to justify [E37]. The stock trades at a demanding P/E of 34, which is a steep premium over the sector benchmark of 24.24x, while its P/B of 2.45x also exceeds the sector benchmark of 2x [E6, E7]. This rich multiple rests on weak underlying profitability, evidenced by a dismal 2.9% ROE and a 10-year median ROE of just 4% [E13, E26]. Furthermore, debt exceeds net worth with a leverage ratio of 1.16x, and total borrowings have climbed to Rs 615 Cr alongside zero free cash flow as of March 2026 [E36, E37, E39]. Institutional sentiment is also cooling, marked by foreign institutional stake contraction and negative money flow, while long-term profit growth paints a grim historical picture with a 10-year compounded profit contraction of -7% and a severe -40% drop over 3 years [E18, E20, E42, E44]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong recent top-line momentum with trailing twelve-month sales growth of 32% and a rules-based screen score of 78 out of 100 [E17, E62].

Conceded: the 10-year compounded profit growth is -7% [E18] and the 3-year profit growth is -40% [E20]. However, focusing solely on historical contractions ignores the explosive recent inflection where trailing twelve-month profit growth has surged by 31% and sales have accelerated by 32% [E17, E21], outperforming the sector median sales growth of 17.4% [E74]. Conceded: debt exceeds net worth at 1.16x leverage [E37]. Nevertheless, this capital is actively funding future capacity rather than sitting idle, evidenced by a massive 91.7% year-on-year increase in capital work-in-progress to Rs 23 Cr [E40], while strong cash conversion of 1.46x proves that reported profits are fully backed by actual cash [E34]. Conceded: foreign institutional holdings contracted slightly and money flow reads negative [E42, E44]. Yet insiders have aggressively accumulated shares—raising promoter ownership by 3.82 percentage points to 61.17% [E41]—demonstrating supreme confidence that eclipses institutional outflows. Finally, while valuation multiples sit above sector benchmarks [E6, E7], a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 1154 per share which provides a tangible 16.6% margin of safety over the market price [E45, E46].

Conceded: promoters increased their stake by 3.82 percentage points to 61.17% [E41], but foreign institutional holdings contracted and institutional money flow is flagged as negative [E42, E44].
